issue_context.title: k_heap_aligned_alloc does not handle a timeout of K_FOREVER correctly
issue_context.body:
When K_FOREVER is passed the return value of z_timeout_end_calc is MAX_UINT64 which equates to -1 when treated as an int64_t.  This causes the end-now check to always return < 0.

The timeout handing code in k_mem_pool_alloc appears to be correct.  k_heap_aligned_alloc should be updated with similar logic.

This was found in Zephyr 2.4, but the issue is still present in current code.
comments: @jshoen Can you submit a PR for fixing this?
I can submit a PR, but may take me some time.  I have not submitted to zephyr before.
Setting this issue to high priority since it is a kernel bug and we definitely want it fixed in this release.

review_comments: Personally I'm a fan of vertical compression; source code gets too long to read in most modern styles.  Semantically my brain reads that like MIN/MAX/CLAMP, where the if() signals "behavior".  But these are going to generate the same code, so I don't see much reason to care.
That being the case I prefer to leave as-is.
Cool with that, thanks for the quick turnaround folks!
